In fact System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in .NET Framework 4.0 and later and in netstandard2.0, and classes and structs are valid targets for it there. Only Assembly as a target was added later. Consumers that build generated code for netstandard2.0 or net472 therefore get no coverage exclusion, which breaks F1 (all generated code decorated) for those targets. Many library consumers multi-target netstandard2.0, so their reports still count generated formatters and resolvers. The README (h1) states the same wrong premise, and the new test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable locks in the unnecessary guard.
